summary:
Hello! We want to present Phyllobytes. 

With Phyllobytes we want to tackle a real problematic in our current world, with a greater focus on Costa Rica and Central America. As extreme rainfall patterns shift, communities, essential services, and infrastructure planners need to understand what is happening in their local areas. 

 Many communities and municipalities lack the time, technical expertise, or resources to access and interpret the information needed to anticipate environmental risks. This project is particularly significant for underserved and often overlooked communities, which continue to experience the impacts of extreme weather events in their everyday lives. 

Phyllobytes is more than a weather dashboard. Originating in Costa Rica, it is a platform built on the belief that Earth observation data should be accessible to everyone. By transforming complex environmental information into clear, meaningful insights, we are making knowledge more accessible and empowering people from smalls communities to better understand our planet. 

We do not want people to have to understand science in order to benefit from it. We want to use science and technology so that everyone can better understand the place where they live.
details:
We chose Costa Rica as a starting point because its geographical diversity highlights the importance of understanding the unique characteristics of each territory. Furthermore, as is the case in many countries around the world, like Central America, such data is often merely presented, without reaching a level of genuine analysis or understanding. Our ultimate goal is to develop an open methodology that can be adapted and implemented in any country and more importantly in any community. 

 Phyllobytes transforms open-source NASA precipitation data into an accessible web-based atlas, allowing users, communities and municipalities to explore the entire country of Costa Rica, as well as the rest of Central America. It grasp historical trends, understand local changes and helps make better decisions using real data. Providing knowledge to help communities prepare for the future, helping places in which this data is not analyzed nor compare. As rainfall patterns and extreme weather conditions evolve and change over the years and decades, these communities are often left facing the consequences  once they are already happening rather than having the information and tools to prepare for them. Understanding environmental patterns should not be a privilege reserved for specialists or institutions with advanced technical resources.

 Through guided visualizations and simplified analysis, users can explore environmental changes, identify rainfall patterns, recognize potential risks, and make more informed decisions. Accessibility is at the heart of this website. For people without a technical background, searching for, interpreting, and comparing satellite data can be intimidating and time consuming. So, we believe this information should be understandable and useful to everyone, regardless of their background, knowledge, or technical experience. 

 By making environmental data easier to access and understand, we aim to empower communities, municipalities, and individuals with the knowledge they need to become more aware, better prepared, and more resilient to the environmental challenges ahead.
